levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Earth Lusca malware family, specifically the KTLVdoor backdoor, has been detected in your network. This backdoor is known for its multiplatform intrusion capabilities, including command and control (C2) communication, lateral movement, exfiltration, and persistence mechanisms. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. **Access the target host:**
   ```bash
   ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5
   ```
2. **List all services:**
   ```bash
   systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   ```
3. **Identify the suspicious service:**
   Look for a service that is not commonly associated with standard system operations. Pay attention to services with unusual names or descriptions.
4. **Final Flag:**
   The suspicious service is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system operations.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the service descriptions for any unusual or unfamiliar entries.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. **Access the target host:**
   ```bash
   ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5
   ```
2. **Identify the suspicious service:**
   ```bash
   systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   ```
3. **Check the service details:**
   ```bash
   systemctl cat <service_name>
   ```
   Replace `<service_name>` with the name of the suspicious service identified in the previous step.
4. **Identify the port:**
   Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service details, which specifies the command launched by the service. The port number is typically an argument to this command.
5. **Final Flag:**
   The network port is `8032`.

hints.title: Third hint title

levels.title: Identify System Information Collection Service
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. **Access the target host:**
   ```bash
   ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5
   ```
2. **List all timers:**
   ```bash
   systemctl list-timers --all
   ```
3. **Identify the suspicious timer:**
   Look for a timer that is not commonly associated with standard system operations. Pay attention to timers with unusual names or descriptions.
4. **Check the timer details:**
   ```bash
   systemctl cat <timer_name>
   ```
   Replace `<timer_name>` with the name of the suspicious timer identified in the previous step.
5. **Identify the associated service:**
   The timer details will specify the service that is triggered by the timer.
6. **Final Flag:**
   The system information collection service is `local-inventory.timer`.
